part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
raw: PART IV HOW THESEUS FELL BY HIS PRIDE

translation.en: Part 4: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
translation.kr: [4부: 오만함으로 몰락한 테세우스]

part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
raw: But that fair Ariadne never came to Athens with her husband.  Some say that Theseus left her sleeping on Naxos among the Cyclades; and that Dionusos the wine-king found her, and took her up into the sky, as you shall see some day in a painting of old Titian’s—one of the most glorious pictures upon earth.  And some say that Dionusos drove away Theseus, and took Ariadne from him by force: but however that may be, in his haste or in his grief, Theseus forgot to put up the white sail.  Now Ægeus his father sat and watched on Sunium day after day, and strained his old eyes across the sea to see the ship afar.  And when he saw the black sail, and not the white one, he gave up Theseus for dead, and in his grief he fell into the sea, and died; so it is called the Ægean to this day.

translation.en: But beautiful Ariadne never reached Athens with her husband.
translation.kr: 하지만 아름다운 아리아드네는 남편과 함께 아테네에 도착하지 못했습니다.

translation.en: Some say Theseus abandoned her while she slept on the island of Naxos.
translation.kr: 어떤 이들은 테세우스가 낙소스섬에서 잠든 그녀를 버려두고 떠났다고 말합니다.

translation.en: Then Dionysus, the god of wine, found her and carried her up to the sky.
translation.kr: 그 후 포도주의 신 디오니소스가 그녀를 발견하여 하늘로 데려갔다는 것입니다.

translation.en: You might see this someday in a famous, glorious painting by Titian.
translation.kr: 언젠가 티치아노가 그린 세상에서 가장 찬란한 명화에서 그 모습을 보실 수 있을 것입니다.

translation.en: Others claim Dionysus drove Theseus away and took Ariadne by force.
translation.kr: 다른 이들은 디오니소스가 테세우스를 쫓아내고 아리아드네를 강제로 빼앗았다고도 합니다.

translation.en: Whatever the truth, in his rush or sorrow, Theseus forgot to hoist the white sail.
translation.kr: 진실이 무엇이든, 테세우스는 서두르거나 슬퍼하느라 하얀 돛을 올리는 것을 잊어버렸습니다.

translation.en: Meanwhile, his father Aegeus sat waiting on the cliffs of Sunium every day.
translation.kr: 한편 그의 아버지 아이게우스는 매일 수니온 절벽에 앉아 기다렸습니다.

translation.en: He strained his old eyes across the sea to spot the ship from afar.
translation.kr: 그는 늙은 눈을 부릅뜨고 바다 너머 멀리서 배가 오는지 지켜보았습니다.

translation.en: When he saw the black sail instead of the white one, he believed his son was dead.
translation.kr: 그가 하얀 돛 대신 검은 돛을 보았을 때, 그는 아들이 죽었다고 생각했습니다.

translation.en: In his overwhelming grief, he threw himself into the sea and died.
translation.kr: 걷잡을 수 없는 슬픔에 빠진 그는 바다에 몸을 던져 목숨을 잃고 말았습니다.

translation.en: That is why those waters are called the Aegean Sea to this day.
translation.kr: 그 바다가 오늘날까지도 아이게우스의 이름을 따서 에게해라고 불리는 이유입니다.

part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
raw: And now Theseus was king of Athens, and he guarded it and ruled it well.

translation.en: Theseus was now the king of Athens, and he protected and ruled it well.
translation.kr: 이제 테세우스는 아테네의 왕이 되어 나라를 훌륭하게 다스리고 보호했습니다.

part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
raw: For he killed the bull of Marathon, which had killed Androgeos, Minos’ son; and he drove back the famous Amazons, the warlike women of the East, when they came from Asia, and conquered all Hellas, and broke into Athens itself.  But Theseus stopped them there, and conquered them, and took Hippolute their queen to be his wife.  Then he went out to fight against the Lapithai, and Peirithoos their famous king: but when the two heroes came face to face they loved each other, and embraced, and became noble friends; so that the friendship of Theseus and Peirithoos is a proverb even now.  And he gathered (so the Athenians say) all the boroughs of the land together, and knit them into one strong people, while before they were all parted and weak: and many another wise thing he did, so that his people honoured him after he was dead, for many a hundred years, as the father of their freedom and their laws.  And six hundred years after his death, in the famous fight at Marathon, men said that they saw the ghost of Theseus, with his mighty brazen club, fighting in the van of battle against the invading Persians, for the country which he loved.  And twenty years after Marathon his bones (they say) were found in Scuros, an isle beyond the sea; and they were bigger than the bones of mortal man. So the Athenians brought them home in triumph; and all the people came out to welcome them; and they built over them a noble temple, and adorned it with sculptures and paintings in which we are told all the noble deeds of Theseus, and the Centaurs, and the Lapithai, and the Amazons; and the ruins of it are standing still.

translation.en: He killed the fierce bull of Marathon that had slain King Minos's son.
translation.kr: 그는 미노스 왕의 아들을 죽였던 마라톤의 사나운 황소를 물리쳤습니다.

translation.en: He also drove back the famous Amazons, the fierce warrior women of the East.
translation.kr: 또한 동방의 용맹한 여전사들인 유명한 아마존 군대도 격퇴했습니다.

translation.en: They had marched from Asia, conquered Greece, and broken right into Athens.
translation.kr: 그들은 아시아에서 진군하여 그리스를 정복하고 아테네까지 쳐들어왔습니다.

translation.en: But Theseus stopped them, defeated their army, and married their queen, Hippolyta.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 그들을 막아내어 물리쳤고, 여왕 히폴리테를 아내로 맞이했습니다.

translation.en: Later, he went to fight the Lapiths and their famous king, Pirithous.
translation.kr: 훗날 그는 라피타이족과 그들의 유명한 왕 피리토오스와 싸우러 나갔습니다.

translation.en: But when the two heroes met face to face, they felt an instant bond.
translation.kr: 하지만 두 영웅이 얼굴을 마주하자 그들은 즉시 깊은 유대감을 느꼈습니다.

translation.en: They embraced and became such great friends that their loyalty is still a proverb today.
translation.kr: 그들은 서로를 껴안고 훌륭한 친구가 되었으며, 그 우정은 오늘날까지도 전설로 남아있습니다.

translation.en: Athenians say Theseus united all the scattered towns into one strong nation.
translation.kr: 아테네 사람들은 테세우스가 흩어진 마을들을 하나로 모아 강한 국가를 만들었다고 말합니다.

translation.en: Before this, they had been divided and weak.
translation.kr: 그 이전에는 모두 분열되어 힘이 없었습니다.

translation.en: He did many other wise things, and his people honored him for centuries after his death.
translation.kr: 그는 수많은 지혜로운 업적을 남겼고, 백성들은 그가 죽은 뒤에도 수백 년 동안 그를 존경했습니다.

translation.en: They remembered him as the father of their freedom and their laws.
translation.kr: 사람들은 그를 자유와 법의 아버지로 기억했습니다.

translation.en: Six hundred years later, at the famous Battle of Marathon, soldiers claimed to see his ghost.
translation.kr: 육백 년 후 벌어진 유명한 마라톤 전투에서 병사들은 그의 유령을 보았다고 주장했습니다.

translation.en: They saw him wielding his mighty bronze club, fighting invading Persians for his beloved country.
translation.kr: 그가 굳센 청동 몽둥이를 휘두르며 사랑하는 조국을 위해 페르시아 침략군에 맞서 싸웠다는 것입니다.

translation.en: Twenty years after that battle, his massive bones were supposedly found on the island of Scyros.
translation.kr: 그 전투로부터 이십 년 후, 바다 너머 스키로스섬에서 그의 거대한 뼈가 발견되었다고 합니다.

translation.en: They were far larger than the bones of any normal mortal man.
translation.kr: 그 뼈는 평범한 인간의 뼈보다 훨씬 더 컸습니다.

translation.en: The Athenians brought his remains home in triumph, and the whole city welcomed them.
translation.kr: 아테네 사람들은 승리에 차서 그의 유해를 고향으로 모셔왔고, 모든 시민이 나와 환영했습니다.

translation.en: They built a grand temple over his tomb, decorated with magnificent sculptures and paintings.
translation.kr: 그들은 무덤 위에 웅장한 신전을 짓고 화려한 조각과 그림으로 장식했습니다.

translation.en: These artworks depicted his brave battles against monsters, centaurs, and the Amazons.
translation.kr: 이 예술품들은 괴물과 켄타우로스, 그리고 아마존에 맞서 싸운 그의 용감한 행적을 담고 있었습니다.

translation.en: The ruins of that glorious temple are still standing today.
translation.kr: 그 찬란했던 신전의 폐허는 지금도 굳건히 서 있습니다.

part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
raw: But why did they find his bones in Scuros?  Why did he not die in peace at Athens, and sleep by his father’s side?  Because after his triumph he grew proud, and broke the laws of God and man.  And one thing worst of all he did, which brought him to his grave with sorrow.  For he went down (they say beneath the earth) with that bold Peirithoos his friend to help him to carry off Persephone, the queen of the world below.  But Peirithoos was killed miserably, in the dark fire-kingdoms under ground; and Theseus was chained to a rock in everlasting pain.  And there he sat for years, till Heracles the mighty came down to bring up the three-headed dog who sits at Pluto’s gate.  So Heracles loosed him from his chain, and brought him up to the light once more.

translation.en: But why were his bones found on the island of Scyros?
translation.kr: 그런데 왜 그의 뼈가 스키로스섬에서 발견되었을까요?

translation.en: Why didn't he die peacefully in Athens and rest beside his father?
translation.kr: 왜 그는 아테네에서 평화롭게 죽어 아버지 곁에 잠들지 못했을까요?

translation.en: It was because his victories made him arrogant, and he broke both human and divine laws.
translation.kr: 승리에 취해 오만해진 그가 신과 인간의 법을 모두 어겼기 때문입니다.

translation.en: He committed one terrible final act that brought him to a sorrowful end.
translation.kr: 그는 결국 자신을 비참한 죽음으로 몰고 간 끔찍한 잘못을 저질렀습니다.

translation.en: He went down into the Underworld with his bold friend Pirithous.
translation.kr: 그는 대담한 친구 피리토오스와 함께 지하 세계로 내려갔습니다.

translation.en: He wanted to help his friend kidnap Persephone, the queen of the dead.
translation.kr: 죽은 자들의 여왕 페르세포네를 납치하려는 친구를 돕기 위해서였습니다.

translation.en: But Pirithous met a miserable death in those dark, fiery underground realms.
translation.kr: 하지만 피리토오스는 그 어둡고 뜨거운 지하 왕국에서 비참하게 목숨을 잃었습니다.

translation.en: Theseus was chained to a rock, cursed to suffer in everlasting pain.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 바위에 사슬로 묶여 영원한 고통을 겪는 저주를 받았습니다.

translation.en: He sat there for years until the mighty Hercules came down to the Underworld.
translation.kr: 그는 강력한 헤라클레스가 지하 세계로 내려올 때까지 몇 년 동안이나 그곳에 묶여 있었습니다.

translation.en: Hercules was there to capture the three-headed dog that guarded the gates of the dead.
translation.kr: 헤라클레스는 죽음의 문을 지키는 머리 셋 달린 개를 잡으러 그곳에 왔습니다.

translation.en: He took pity on Theseus, shattered his magical chains, and brought him back to the sunlight.
translation.kr: 그는 테세우스를 가엾게 여겨 마법 사슬을 부수고 그를 다시 햇빛 속으로 데려왔습니다.

part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
raw: But when he came back his people had forgotten him, and Castor and Polydeuces, the sons of the wondrous Swan, had invaded his land, and carried off his mother Aithra for a slave, in revenge for a grievous wrong.

translation.en: But when Theseus returned, his people had already forgotten him.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스가 돌아왔을 때, 백성들은 이미 그를 잊고 있었습니다.

translation.en: The fierce twin brothers, Castor and Pollux, had invaded his kingdom.
translation.kr: 사나운 쌍둥이 형제인 카스토르와 폴룩스가 그의 왕국을 침략했던 것입니다.

translation.en: They kidnapped his mother Aethra and made her a slave to avenge a terrible wrong.
translation.kr: 그들은 끔찍한 악행에 복수하기 위해 그의 어머니 아이트라를 납치하여 노예로 삼았습니다.

part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
raw: So the fair land of Athens was wasted, and another king ruled it, who drove out Theseus shamefully, and he fled across the sea to Scuros.  And there he lived in sadness, in the house of Lucomedes the king, till Lucomedes killed him by treachery, and there was an end of all his labours.

translation.en: The beautiful land of Athens was ruined, and a new king ruled in his place.
translation.kr: 아름다운 아테네 땅은 폐허가 되었고, 새로운 왕이 그의 자리를 대신하여 다스렸습니다.

translation.en: This new king chased Theseus away in disgrace, forcing him to flee across the sea to Scyros.
translation.kr: 이 새로운 왕은 테세우스를 불명예스럽게 쫓아냈고, 그는 바다 건너 스키로스섬으로 도망쳐야 했습니다.

translation.en: He lived there in deep sadness at the court of King Lycomedes.
translation.kr: 그는 리코메데스 왕의 궁전에서 깊은 슬픔에 빠져 살았습니다.

translation.en: Eventually, Lycomedes murdered him through cruel treachery, putting an end to all his heroic labors.
translation.kr: 결국 리코메데스 왕이 잔인한 배신으로 그를 살해하면서 그의 모든 영웅적인 업적도 끝이 났습니다.

part: Part IV: How Theseus Fell by His Pride
raw: So it is still, my children, and so it will be to the end.  In those old Greeks, and in us also, all strength and virtue come from God.  But if men grow proud and self-willed, and misuse God’s fair gifts, He lets them go their own ways, and fall pitifully, that the glory may be His alone. God help us all, and give us wisdom, and courage to do noble deeds! but God keep pride from us when we have done them, lest we fall, and come to shame!

translation.en: And so it remains today, my children, and so it will be until the end of time.
translation.kr: 아이들아, 이것은 오늘날에도 마찬가지이며 세상 끝날까지 변하지 않을 진리입니다.

translation.en: For the ancient Greeks, just as for us, all strength and goodness come from above.
translation.kr: 고대 그리스인들에게나 우리에게나 모든 힘과 선함은 하늘에서 옵니다.

translation.en: But if people grow arrogant and selfish, misusing their wonderful gifts, they are left to their own paths.
translation.kr: 하지만 사람들이 오만하고 이기적으로 변하여 훌륭한 재능을 남용한다면, 결국 자신의 길을 잃게 됩니다.

translation.en: They will fall pitifully, proving that true glory does not belong to mortals.
translation.kr: 그들은 비참하게 몰락하여 진정한 영광이 인간의 것이 아님을 증명하게 될 것입니다.

translation.en: May we all find the wisdom and courage to perform noble deeds!
translation.kr: 우리 모두가 숭고한 일을 해낼 수 있는 지혜와 용기를 얻기를 바랍니다!

translation.en: But may we also be saved from toxic pride, so we do not fall into ruin and bitter shame.
translation.kr: 하지만 우리가 파멸과 쓰디쓴 수치심에 빠지지 않도록 끔찍한 오만함으로부터 구원받기를 기도합니다.
